title: Anomaly Detection Baseline: Can Unsupervised Outlier Methods Match Supervised CoT Monitors?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If unsupervised methods match supervised monitors, it removes the labeling bottleneck entirely. This directly enables monitoring in domains where labeled misalignment data is unavailable. High practical impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses standard scikit-learn anomaly detectors (isolation forest, one-class SVM) on embeddings. MALT provides labeled data. Computing embeddings from a small encoder model is straightforward. Well within beginner ML scope with CS background.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single clear experiment: embed CoT traces, train anomaly detector, compare AUROC to published baseline. One dataset, two standard methods, one comparison metric. Fits comfortably in 30 hours.
